question: Why do finite nondegenerate higher-time-derivative Lagrangians develop an Ostrogradsky instability, and how can degeneracy-generated constraints remove the offending degree of freedom?

key_findings.claim: A nondegenerate second-derivative Lagrangian produces a Hamiltonian linear in an unconstrained physical momentum and therefore unbounded above and below.
key_findings.evidence: The thesis derives the result both by diagonalizing a quadratic example into healthy and negative-kinetic variables and by introducing an auxiliary coordinate and Lagrange multiplier, exposing the unrestricted momentum in the general Hamiltonian.

key_findings.claim: Degeneracy is useful only through the constraint chain it induces, not merely because a Hessian determinant vanishes.
key_findings.evidence: A singular kinetic matrix gives a primary constraint on phase space. Requiring its preservation under Hamiltonian evolution can generate a secondary constraint; in the coupled second-order cases studied, that secondary constraint solves for the momentum that otherwise enters the Hamiltonian linearly.

key_findings.claim: For the analyzed single-variable and one-regular-variable second-order systems, all enumerated degenerate kinetic cases remove the apparent Ostrogradsky mode.
key_findings.evidence: A degenerate single-variable model reduces to a first-order equivalent system. In the coupled case, the author partitions the Hessian degeneracy condition into three cases and shows either reduction or a primary-secondary constraint pair that fixes the dangerous momentum and remaining multiplier.

key_findings.claim: The work is a pedagogical bachelor thesis synthesizing established results, and its general n-th derivative discussion is a heuristic outline rather than a completed theorem.
key_findings.evidence: The second-order calculations explicitly follow Ganz and Noui. Section 5 only counts auxiliary variables and anticipated constraints, then warns that one degeneracy may leave other linear momenta; no field-theory, quantum, gauge, or full degree-of-freedom classification is performed.

method.core_idea: Translate higher-derivative mechanics into first-order constrained Hamiltonian systems and track primary and secondary constraints with the Dirac algorithm.
method.mechanism: Auxiliary coordinates represent successive time derivatives, Lagrange multipliers enforce their relations, the Legendre Hessian diagnoses degeneracy, and Poisson-bracket consistency determines whether constraints remove linear canonical momenta.
assumptions: The Lagrangians have finitely many time derivatives and sufficient smoothness.
The studied finite-dimensional mechanical examples represent the essential classical instability.
Generic Poisson brackets needed to fix multipliers are nonzero.
Eliminating the displayed linear momentum removes the Ostrogradsky mode, though not every possible instability.

techniques.role: Rewrites higher-order dynamics as a constrained first-order system.
Detects whether velocities can be inverted into canonical momenta.
Uses time preservation of primary constraints to find secondary constraints and fix multipliers.

evaluations.metric: signs of kinetic terms and Hamiltonian boundedness
evaluations.result: Both diagonalization and constrained Hamiltonian reduction exhibit the same ghost.

evaluations.setting: General second-order coordinate coupled to one regular coordinate
evaluations.metric: rank of kinetic matrix, constraint count, and restriction of the linear momentum
evaluations.result: Nondegenerate cases retain the ghost; all analyzed degenerate cases produce sufficient constraints to remove the displayed Ostrogradsky momentum.

limitations: This is an expository undergraduate thesis whose principal second-order results follow prior work rather than a new classification.
The n-th-order section stops before explicit consistency calculations or necessary-and-sufficient degeneracy conditions.
Finite-dimensional classical mechanics does not capture gauge constraints, spatial derivatives, covariance, or quantum vacuum decay in field theory.
Absence of an Ostrogradsky ghost does not prove that the final Hamiltonian is bounded or otherwise physically healthy.
failure_modes: A degenerate Hessian produces too few independent secondary constraints to eliminate every linear momentum.
A hidden gauge symmetry changes the first-/second-class constraint count assumed in the generic analysis.
Gradient or potential instabilities remain after the Ostrogradsky degree of freedom is removed.
Quantization reintroduces negative norm, nonunitarity, or an unbounded spectrum not diagnosed by the classical exercise.
reusable_insights: Higher derivatives alone are not the decisive diagnosis; count independent propagating degrees of freedom after all constraints close.
A claim of ghost freedom should display the complete primary-secondary constraint algebra, not only Hessian degeneracy.
Removing one linear momentum is necessary but not a certificate of total stability.
Pedagogical derivations should clearly distinguish synthesis from original theorem claims.
open_questions: What degeneracy hierarchy is necessary and sufficient to remove every Ostrogradsky mode at arbitrary derivative order?
How does the constraint count change for gauge and generally covariant theories?
Which degenerate higher-derivative theories remain stable after quantum corrections?
Can automated symbolic tools reliably complete Dirac analyses for realistic field theories?

competitive_landscape.title: The Theorem of Ostrogradsky
competitive_landscape.difference: Woodard gives an established modern derivation and surveys proposed evasions for interacting continuum theories. The thesis offers a gentler worked constraint tutorial but no broader theorem.

competitive_landscape.title: Reconsidering the Ostrogradsky theorem: Higher-derivatives Lagrangians, Ghosts and Degeneracy
competitive_landscape.difference: Ganz and Noui already extend the theorem to several variables, degeneracy, quantum aspects, and covariant theories. The reviewed thesis explicitly bases its second-order analyses on this paper and substantially narrows its scope.

competitive_landscape.title: Ghost from constraints: a generalization of Ostrogradsky theorem
competitive_landscape.difference: Aoki and Motohashi derive ghost criteria for auxiliary variables and nonholonomic constraints even without higher-order equations. The thesis uses constraints only to explain the standard higher-derivative setting.

competitive_landscape.title: Quantum Ostrogradsky theorem
competitive_landscape.difference: Motohashi and Suyama prove unboundedness persists after quantization for nondegenerate higher-derivative field theories. The thesis is purely classical and cannot support quantum health claims.

competitive_landscape.title: Dark Energy and Modified Gravity in Degenerate Higher-Order Scalar-Tensor (DHOST) theories: a review
competitive_landscape.difference: Langlois reviews the classified DHOST families and phenomenological constraints. The thesis supplies only the mechanical constraint intuition that such field-theory classifications operationalize.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after primary-source comparison: the thesis is a clear educational reconstruction of Ostrogradsky's theorem and the Dirac-constraint escape route. It should not be presented as an original ghost-free classification: its direct source is broader, and its arbitrary-order section is explicitly unfinished.
reviewer_notes: Read all 25 pages, checking the negative-energy example, auxiliary-variable derivation, Dirac formalism, all coupled degeneracy cases, general-order outline, and conclusion. Five primary arXiv sources were checked on 2026-08-23.
